mcqs.learning_point: Classify matter into elements, compounds and mixtures
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares elements, compounds and mixtures?

options.A: Elements consist of two or more types of atoms chemically combined; compounds consist of only one type of atom; mixtures are chemically combined substances.
options.B: Elements are pure substances made of only one kind of atom; compounds are pure substances formed by chemical combination of two or more elements; mixtures are physical combinations of two or more substances that retain their individual identities.
options.C: Elements and compounds are both mixtures; only mixtures are pure substances.
options.D: Elements are always gases; compounds are always liquids; mixtures are always solids.

mcqs.answer: Elements are pure substances made of only one kind of atom; compounds are pure substances formed by chemical combination of two or more elements; mixtures are physical combinations of two or more substances that retain their individual identities.
mcqs.explanation: Elements contain only one type of atom, compounds are formed when two or more different elements combine chemically, and mixtures are physical blends where each component keeps its own identity. Option B states this correctly; the other options contain factual errors.

mcqs.question: In a competitive‑exam style question, which of the following is a heterogeneous mixture?

options.B: A solution of common salt in water

mcqs.explanation: Soil consists of visible particles of different substances (sand, organic matter, minerals) that are not uniformly distributed, making it heterogeneous. Air, a salt solution, and brass are homogeneous (uniform) at the macroscopic level. Hence option C is correct.

mcqs.question: Matter can be defined as:

options.A: Anything that has mass and occupies space
options.B: Anything that can be seen with the naked eye
options.C: Anything that is solid at room temperature

mcqs.answer: Anything that has mass and occupies space
mcqs.explanation: The fundamental definition of matter is that it possesses mass and takes up space (volume). Options B, C, and D describe specific attributes but do not encompass the full definition.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a chemical property of a substance?
mcqs.explanation: Chemical properties describe how a substance interacts with other substances; reactivity with acid indicates a chemical change. Melting point, density, and color are physical properties because they can be observed without changing the chemical identity.

mcqs.question: When an ice cube melts to water at room temperature, the process is best described as:
mcqs.explanation: Melting involves a change of state from solid to liquid without altering the chemical composition of H₂O; therefore it is a physical change. No new substances are formed, so options A, C, and D are incorrect.

mcqs.learning_point: Classify matter into elements, compounds and mixtures
mcqs.question: A sample of pure copper metal, a bottle of sugar solution, and a mixture of sand and iron filings are placed on a table. Classify each as element, compound, or mixture.

options.A: Copper – element, sugar solution – compound, sand‑iron – mixture
options.B: Copper – element, sugar solution – mixture, sand‑iron – compound
options.C: Copper – compound, sugar solution – element, sand‑iron – mixture
options.D: Copper – mixture, sugar solution – element, sand‑iron – compound

mcqs.answer: Copper – element, sugar solution – compound, sand‑iron – mixture
mcqs.explanation: Copper consists of only Cu atoms → element. Sugar dissolved in water forms a uniform chemical combination of C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ and H₂O → compound (solution). Sand and iron filings retain their individual identities → mixture. Option A correctly matches each.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a homogeneous mixture?
mcqs.explanation: Air is a uniform mixture of gases (nitrogen, oxygen, etc.) at the macroscopic level, making it homogeneous. Soil, concrete, and oil‑water mixtures are heterogeneous because their components are not uniformly distributed.

mcqs.question: A student says that a substance that can be measured by a balance and occupies space is called matter. Which statement best reflects this definition?

options.A: Matter is anything that can be seen with the naked eye.
options.B: Matter is anything that has mass and takes up space.
options.D: Matter is only substances that undergo chemical change.

mcqs.answer: Matter is anything that has mass and takes up space.
mcqs.explanation: The definition of matter emphasizes two fundamental attributes: mass (measurable by a balance) and volume (occupying space). Option B captures both attributes accurately; the other options are either too restrictive or unrelated.
